components.name: Avatar
components.purpose: A person or thing as a small round picture, falling back to initials, then to an icon.
components.use: Beside a name in a list, a comment or a menu, and in an AvatarGroup for the people on something.
components.avoid: For a logo or a photo that is content, use an img; for a status on the avatar, wrap it in a Chip.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; an avatar is not a hit target, so put it in a Button or Link for one.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: src
props.description: The image's address.

props.name: alt
props.description: Who or what it shows ("Ada Lovelace"): the image's alt, and the source of the initials.

props.name: text
props.description: Text in place of the initials from alt, such as a short code.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon shown with neither image nor name; without it, a silhouette.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` 24 px, `md` 32 px, `lg` 40 px. In an AvatarGroup, the group's size wins.

components.notes:
It shows `src` when it loads. With no `src`, or when the image fails (also
when it failed before an island hydrated), it shows initials: `text` if
given, else the first letters of the first and last words of `alt`
("Ada Lovelace" is AL). With neither, it shows `icon`, a Lucide name, or
without one a silhouette it draws itself (so no icon ships for it).

`alt` names it: the image's alt text, or, for initials and icon, the
avatar's `aria-label` with `role="img"`. Without `alt` it is decorative.
`size` is `sm` (24 px), `md` (32 px) or `lg` (40 px); in an AvatarGroup the
group's size wins.

examples.name: basic
examples.title: Basic
examples.source:
<script setup vapor lang="ts">
import { Avatar, Stack } from '@weft/ui'

// An inline drawing, so the example needs no network.
const picture =
  'data:image/svg+xml,' +
  encodeURIComponent('<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 32 32"><rect width="32" height="32" fill="#6B7D2E"/><circle cx="16" cy="13" r="6" fill="#F8FAFC"/></svg>')
</script>

<template>
  <!-- An image, initials from alt, then an icon when there is neither. -->
  <Stack direction="row" :gap="2" align="center">
    <Avatar :src="picture" alt="Ada Lovelace" />
    <Avatar alt="Grace Hopper" />
    <Avatar />
  </Stack>
</template>

components.name: AvatarGroup
components.purpose: Avatars overlapping in a row, showing the first few and counting the rest.
components.use: For the people on a project, a thread or a document, where the faces matter more than the names.
components.avoid: For a list a person reads name by name, use a list with an Avatar beside each name.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; the group is not a hit target.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; set max so the row fits the narrowest place it appears.

props.name: max
props.description: How many avatars to show; the rest are counted. Unset or 0 shows all.

props.name: size
props.description: The size of every avatar in the group.

components.notes:
Put Avatars in its default slot. With `max`, the first `max` show and a last
avatar counts the rest (`+3`); without it every avatar shows. `size` sizes
every avatar in the group.

It is a `group`: name it with an `aria-label` ("Project members"). Avatars
join the group in the order they render, on the server and in the browser
alike, so the count hydrates as rendered.

const team = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov']

components.name: Badge
components.purpose: A short label for a status, a category or a count, drawn in a tone.
components.use: Beside a title or in a table cell, to say a state at a glance (Paid, Failed, Beta, 3).
components.avoid: For something a person can press or remove, use Button; for an indicator on the corner of an icon or avatar, use Chip.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; a badge is not a hit target.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; a badge does not wrap.

props.name: label
props.description: The badge's text; the default slot replaces it.

props.name: variant
props.description: `solid` to stand out, `soft` and `outline` to sit quietly beside text, `ghost` for tone alone.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour and what it says: `success` for done, `danger` for failed.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the label; alone, the badge is square.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: A Lucide icon after the label.

components.notes:
`variant` is `solid`, `soft`, `outline` or `ghost`; `tone` is `neutral`,
`primary`, `danger`, `warning` or `success`; `size` is `sm`, `md` or `lg`.
Give the text as `label` or as the default slot. Icons are decorative, so the
text must carry the meaning; with only an icon the badge is square and needs
an `aria-label`.

components.name: Button
components.purpose: A button that runs an action, or a link drawn as a button when it has `to`.
components.use: For the actions on a page, a form's submit, a dialog's confirm; solid for the one main action, soft, outline or ghost for the others.
components.avoid: For moving to another page within running text, use Link; for a choice that stays on or off, use a switch or checkbox.

adapts.input: On touch its hit area grows to at least 44 px (--weft-hit-min) through a pseudo-element, so its drawn size and the layout stay the same; hover colours apply only where the device can hover.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; set block to fill a narrow column.

props.name: label
props.description: The button's text; the default slot replaces it.

props.name: variant
props.description: `solid` for the main action, `soft` and `outline` for secondary ones, `ghost` for the quietest.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour and what it says: `danger` for destructive actions.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`: the drawn height, which touch does not change.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the label; alone, the button is square and needs an `aria-label`.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: A Lucide icon after the label.

props.name: loading
props.description: Work in progress: shows a spinner, sets `aria-busy` and blocks activation, keeping width and focus.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: a button is natively disabled; a link loses its address.

props.name: block
props.description: Fill the width of the container.

props.name: to
props.description: An address: the button renders as an `<a>` that goes there (rel="noopener" when it is another site).

props.name: type
props.description: The native button type; `submit` submits its form. Ignored with `to`.

emits.name: click
emits.description: Pressed by mouse, touch or keyboard; never while loading or disabled.

components.notes:
`variant` is `solid`, `soft`, `outline` or `ghost`; `tone` is `neutral`,
`primary`, `danger`, `warning` or `success`; `size` is `sm`, `md` or `lg`.
Give the text as `label` or as the default slot. With only an `icon` the
button is square: give it an `aria-label`.

**Loading** shows a spinner over the content, which stays in place (hidden),
so the button keeps its width. It sets `aria-busy="true"` and
`aria-disabled="true"`, and blocks activation by mouse, keyboard and form
submit, but stays focusable, so a keyboard user does not lose their place.

**Disabled** is the native `disabled` attribute on a button. With `to` the
button is an `<a>`; disabled, it has no address and is announced as a
disabled link.

**Keyboard:** a native button, so Enter and Space press it; as a link, Enter
follows it. Focus shows the theme's focus ring.

`click` is emitted only when the button is pressed while neither loading nor
disabled. `type` defaults to `button`, so a Button inside a form submits it
only with `type="submit"`.

examples.source:
<script setup vapor lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { Button, Stack } from '@weft/ui'

const saving = ref(false)
function save() {
  saving.value = true
  setTimeout(() => (saving.value = false), 1500)
}
</script>

<template>
  <!-- Loading keeps the width and focus, and blocks further presses. -->
  <Stack direction="row" :gap="2">
    <Button label="Save changes" icon="save" :loading="saving" @click="save" />
    <Button label="Disabled" disabled />
  </Stack>
</template>

components.name: Card
components.purpose: A bordered surface holding related content, with an optional header, actions and footer.
components.use: To group a few things that belong together, a plan, a summary, a small form, so they read as one unit.
components.avoid: For a page region with a heading, use Section; for content that needs a focused task, use a dialog.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; the card is not interactive itself.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; header actions wrap under the title when they do not fit.

props.name: padding
props.description: Inner space, from the spacing scale; 0 for edge-to-edge content.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render, for semantics: `article`, `li`, `section`.

components.notes:
`padding` takes 0, 2, 3, 4 or 6 from the spacing scale; use 0 for edge-to-edge
content such as an image or a table. `as` renders another element, such as
`article` or `li`.

components.name: Chip
components.purpose: A small indicator, a dot or a short count, on the corner of what it wraps.
components.use: For unread counts on an icon, online status on an avatar, a mark that something changed.
components.avoid: For a status in a line of text, use Badge.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; the indicator is not a hit target, the wrapped content is.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: text
props.description: A short count or mark inside the indicator; without it the indicator is a dot.

props.name: label
props.description: What the indicator means, for assistive technology ("3 unread messages"); the drawn indicator is then hidden from it.

props.name: tone
props.description: The indicator's colour and what it says.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: position
props.description: Which corner: `top-end`, `bottom-end`, `top-start` or `bottom-start`.

props.name: inset
props.description: Sit inside the corner rather than across it, for round content such as an avatar.

props.name: show
props.description: Show the indicator; false hides it and keeps the content.

components.notes:
Wrap the content in the default slot. `text` puts a short count or mark in
the indicator; without it the indicator is a dot. `position` is logical
(`top-end`, `bottom-end`, `top-start`, `bottom-start`), so `top-end` is the
top right in a left-to-right document and the top left in a right-to-left
one. `inset` keeps the indicator inside the corner, for round content.
`show` hides it, keeping the content.

Give `label` ("3 unread messages") to say what the indicator means: it is
read to assistive technology and the drawn indicator is hidden from it.

components.name: Container
components.purpose: Centres content at the page width, with inline padding.
components.use: Around the content of a landing page band (a hero, a feature grid, a footer) whose background runs full width.
components.avoid: For an app page with a title and actions, use Page, which also sets the width; for grouping things, use Card or Section.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: On landing its width is capped at the page width (--weft-page-max, 1200 px in the shipped themes); in an app it runs full width.
adapts.width: Its inline padding grows with the room around it, from 16 px to 32 px, without a breakpoint.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render, for semantics: `section`, `header`, `footer`.

components.notes: `as` renders another element, such as `section`, `header` or `footer`.

components.name: Divider
components.purpose: A thin rule that separates content, across or alongside it.
components.use: Between groups of content that need a visible break, in a menu, a card or a toolbar.
components.avoid: For a rule with a label or icon, use Separator; for space alone, use the gap of a Stack or Grid; for a new titled part, use Section.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal` separates stacked content; `vertical` separates content in a row.

components.notes:
Horizontal is an `hr`; vertical is an element with `role="separator"` and
`aria-orientation="vertical"`, which stretches to the height of its row.

examples.name: basic
examples.title: Basic

components.name: Grid
components.purpose: Lays its children out in equal columns, as many as its own width allows.
components.use: For tiles, cards and stat blocks that should reflow from one column to several as the space grows.
components.avoid: For a single column or row, use Stack; for tabular data, use a table.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Measured from the grid itself, not the window, so a grid in a side panel stays narrow on a large screen; by default 1 column narrow (under 640 px), 2 regular (under 1024 px) and 3 wide.

props.name: cols
props.type: number | { narrow?: number; regular?: number; wide?: number }
props.description: Columns: one number for every width, or one per width class of the grid's own width.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between cells, from the spacing scale (`--weft-space-*`).

components.notes:
`cols` is a fixed number or one per width class, `{ narrow, regular, wide }`.
A width left out falls back to the nearest smaller one given, else to the
default for it.

components.name: Icon
components.purpose: A Lucide icon by name, drawn as an inline SVG in the current text colour.
components.use: Wherever an icon helps recognition, beside a label or, with a label of its own, standing alone; Weft components take the same names in their icon prop.
components.avoid: For pictures and logos, use an img; never let an icon alone carry meaning without a label.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; an icon is not a hit target, so put it in a Button or Link for one.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; without a size it scales with the surrounding text.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: name
props.description: The Lucide icon's name, as on lucide.dev: `trash`, `chevron-down`.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` 16 px, `md` 20 px, `lg` 24 px; without it the icon is 1.25em, sized with the text.

props.name: label
props.description: What the icon means, for an icon that stands alone; without it the icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

components.notes:
Names are Lucide's, as listed on lucide.dev/icons: `trash`, `chevron-down`.
Only the icons a build uses ship: the build finds static names in templates
(`name="trash"`, `icon="plus"`) and `icon: '…'` properties in scripts, and
fails with a sentence naming the file for a name Lucide does not have. Names
made at run time go in the `icons` option of `weftIcons()`.

Without `label` the icon is decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`); with one it is
an image with that accessible name (`role="img"`). `size` is `sm` (16 px),
`md` (20 px) or `lg` (24 px); without it the icon is 1.25em.

components.name: Island
components.purpose: Renders a component on the server and makes it interactive in the browser, on load, when idle, when visible or when a media query matches.
components.use: For the few interactive parts of an otherwise static page, a counter, a form, a menu, so only they ship JavaScript.
components.avoid: For content that never changes in the browser, render the component directly; a page with no island ships no script at all.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; the island's component adapts as it would anywhere.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: when
props.description: When the browser hydrates it: at `load`, when `idle`, when `visible`, or when `media` matches.

props.name: media
props.description: The media query for `when="media"`, such as `(min-width: 1024px)`.

props.name: component
props.description: The `<script setup>` SFC to render and hydrate; its file name is the island's id.

props.name: props
props.description: Props for the component, sent to the browser as JSON.

components.notes:
The component must be a `<script setup>` single-file component: its file name
is the island's id. `props` travel to the browser as JSON, so they may hold
only strings, finite numbers, booleans, null, arrays and plain objects; the
build refuses anything else with a sentence naming the prop. `when="media"`
needs a `media` query. Ids from `useId` inside an island are counted per
island, so they match between the server and the browser.

Ids are counted by the island's position among the page's islands, the
same on the server (render order) and in the browser (document order). So an
island inside a `<Teleport>`, whose markup lands elsewhere in the document,
is not supported: its position, and so its ids, would differ.

examples.name: basic
examples.title: Basic
examples.source:
<script setup vapor lang="ts">
import { Island, Page } from '@weft/ui'
import Counter from './Counter.vue'
</script>

<template>
  <Page title="Static page, one interactive part">
    <Island when="visible" :component="Counter" :props="{ start: 0 }" />
  </Page>
</template>

components.name: Kbd
components.purpose: A key on the keyboard, for showing shortcuts.
components.use: In help text, menus and tooltips, one Kbd per key of a shortcut.
components.avoid: For code or a value to copy, use a code element.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; show shortcuts only where a keyboard is likely, which the page decides.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: value
props.description: The key: a character (`K`) or a name with a symbol (`command`, `shift`, `option`, `enter`, `backspace`, `tab`, `arrowup`…). The default slot replaces it.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

components.notes:
`value` is a character (`K`) or a key name. Names with a symbol draw the
symbol and say the name to assistive technology, which reads symbols poorly:
`command` (⌘), `shift` (⇧), `option` (⌥), `enter` (↵), `backspace` (⌫),
`tab` (⇥) and the arrows `arrowup`, `arrowdown`, `arrowleft`, `arrowright`.
Any other value is drawn as given. It draws what it is told and never guesses
the reader's operating system, so the server and browser agree. The default
slot replaces the value.

examples.title: Basic

components.name: Link
components.purpose: A link to another page or site, marking itself when it is the current page.
components.use: For navigation, in running text, in a list of pages or a footer.
components.avoid: For an action that changes something, use Button; for a link that should look like a button, use Button with to.

adapts.input: On touch its hit area grows to at least 44 px (--weft-hit-min) through a pseudo-element, without changing the text; hover styles apply only where the device can hover.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: to
props.description: The address.

props.name: href
props.description: The address, for those who write links as HTML does; `to` wins.

props.name: external
props.description: Another site: adds rel="noopener". Unset, an address with a scheme and host (`https://…`, `//…`) is external.

props.name: target
props.description: Where to open it, as the native attribute: `_blank` for a new tab.

props.name: rel
props.description: The native rel; `noopener` is added for an external link.

props.name: active
props.description: This link is the current page: sets aria-current="page". Unset, the link compares its address with the browser's.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: no address, so not focusable, and announced as a disabled link.

emits.name: click
emits.description: Followed by mouse, touch or keyboard; never while disabled.

components.notes:
An external link (an address with a scheme and host, `https://…` or `//…`,
or any with `external`) gets `rel="noopener"`, added to any `rel` you give.
`target` passes through as the native attribute.

The link to the page the browser is on gets `aria-current="page"`. It is
worked out in the browser after mounting, so the server's markup and the
first client render agree; on a page with no JavaScript the server cannot
know, so set `active` where the layout knows the current page. `active`
always wins over the comparison.

**Disabled:** no address, so it leaves the tab order; announced as a disabled
link (`role="link"`, `aria-disabled="true"`); a click does nothing.

**Keyboard:** a native anchor, so Tab reaches it and Enter follows it.

examples.name: current-page
examples.title: Current page
examples.source:
<script setup vapor lang="ts">
import { Link, Stack } from '@weft/ui'
</script>

<template>
  <!-- In the browser a Link marks itself when it is the current page; active says so on the server too. -->
  <nav aria-label="Account">
    <Stack direction="row" :gap="4">
      <Link to="/account" active>Profile</Link>
      <Link to="/account/billing">Billing</Link>
      <Link to="/account/team" disabled>Team</Link>
    </Stack>
  </nav>
</template>

components.name: Page
components.purpose: The main landmark of a page, with its title, description, actions and content.
components.use: Once per page, as the outermost layout component, so the page has one main, one h1 and the surface's width and spacing.
components.avoid: For a titled part inside a page, use Section; for a box of related content, use Card.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: On landing the content is centred at up to 1200 px with wider gaps between sections; on app it fills the width with tighter gaps.
adapts.width: Nothing changes in the component itself; the header's actions wrap under the title when they do not fit beside it.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's heading, rendered as its h1.

props.name: description
props.description: A line under the title saying what the page is for.

components.notes:
The `title` renders as the page's `h1`. Give the `header` slot to replace the
title and description with your own markup, and the `actions` slot for
buttons beside them.

examples.name: basic
examples.title: Basic

components.name: Progress
components.purpose: A bar showing how far a task has got, or that it is under way when that is unknown.
components.use: For uploads, imports, multi-step work and quotas, where the reader waits or watches.
components.avoid: For a short wait inside a control, use Spinner; for loading content, use Skeleton.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; the bar fills the width it is given.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: How far along, from 0 to `max`; `null` or unset for unknown (indeterminate).

props.name: max
props.description: The value at completion.

props.name: label
props.description: What it measures, for assistive technology ("Uploading report.pdf").

props.name: tone
props.description: The bar's colour and what it says.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`: the bar's thickness.

props.name: status
props.description: Show the percentage beside the bar (determinate only).

components.notes:
Bind the value with `v-model` (or `model-value`), from 0 to `max` (100);
values outside are clamped. `null` or no value is indeterminate: a bar that
sweeps, which stands still at full length, dimmed, under reduced motion.
`status` shows the percentage beside the bar.

It is a `progressbar` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and, when
determinate, `aria-valuenow`. Name it with `label` ("Uploading report.pdf")
or an `aria-labelledby`. The bar fills along the inline direction, so from
the right in a right-to-left document.

examples.name: basic
examples.title: Basic
examples.source:
<script setup vapor lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { Progress, Stack } from '@weft/ui'

const uploaded = ref(64)
</script>

<template>
  <Stack :gap="4">
    <Progress v-model="uploaded" label="Uploading report.pdf" status />
    <!-- No value: indeterminate. -->
    <Progress label="Preparing the export" tone="neutral" size="sm" />
  </Stack>
</template>

components.name: Section
components.purpose: A titled part of a page, with an optional description and actions.
components.use: To split a page into named parts, each with an h2, such as Billing and Members on a settings page.
components.avoid: For the page itself, use Page; for a bordered box, use Card.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; the space between sections comes from Page.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; the actions wrap under the title when they do not fit beside it.

props.name: title
props.description: The section's heading, rendered as an h2.

props.name: description
props.description: A line under the title.

components.notes: The `title` renders as an `h2`.

examples.name: basic
examples.title: Basic

components.name: Separator
components.purpose: A rule that separates content, with an optional label or icon in its middle.
components.use: Between groups of content that need a named break, such as "or" between two sign-in methods, or a date in a feed.
components.avoid: For a plain rule, use Divider; for space alone, use the gap of a Stack or Grid; for a new titled part, use Section.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; the label follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: label
props.description: Text in the middle of the rule ("or"); the default slot replaces it.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon in the middle of the rule, before the label.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal` between stacked content; `vertical` between content in a row.

props.name: decorative
props.description: Only visual: hidden from assistive technology, for a rule that separates nothing a reader needs told about.

components.notes:
`label` (or the default slot) and `icon` sit between two lines. It is a
`separator` with `aria-orientation`, named by `label`; `decorative` hides it
from assistive technology (`role="none"`), for a rule that separates nothing
a reader needs told about. `orientation="vertical"` stretches to the height
of its row.

examples.title: Basic
examples.source:
<script setup vapor lang="ts">
import { Button, Separator, Stack } from '@weft/ui'
</script>

<template>
  <Stack :gap="3">
    <Button block label="Continue with email" icon="mail" />
    <Separator label="or" />
    <Button block label="Continue with a passkey" variant="outline" />
  </Stack>
</template>

components.name: Skeleton
components.purpose: A placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading.
components.use: Where text, an avatar or a card will appear, so the layout does not jump when it arrives.
components.avoid: For a wait with no shape to show, use Spinner; when the progress is known, use Progress.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; its default height is one line of the surface's text.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; without a width it fills its container.

props.name: width
props.description: Any CSS length; without it, the full width.

props.name: height
props.description: Any CSS length; without it, one line of text (1em).

props.name: circle
props.description: A circle, for an avatar; set width and height alike.

components.notes:
`width` and `height` take any CSS length; without them it is the full width
and one line (1em) high. `circle` makes it round, for an avatar.

It pulses, and stands still under `prefers-reduced-motion`. It is hidden
from assistive technology: set `aria-busy="true"` on the region that is
loading, and remove it when the content arrives.

examples.name: basic
examples.title: Basic
examples.source:
<script setup vapor lang="ts">
import { Skeleton, Stack } from '@weft/ui'
</script>

<template>
  <!-- The loading region says so with aria-busy; the skeletons are decorative. -->
  <Stack direction="row" :gap="3" align="center" aria-busy="true">
    <Skeleton circle width="40px" height="40px" />
    <Stack :gap="2" style="flex: 1">
      <Skeleton width="40%" />
      <Skeleton width="80%" />
    </Stack>
  </Stack>
</template>

components.name: Spinner
components.purpose: A turning ring for work in progress of unknown length.
components.use: Inside something that is loading, or alone where content will appear; Button shows one itself when loading.
components.avoid: When the progress is known, use Progress; for the shape of content still loading, use Skeleton.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; without a size it scales with the text.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` 16 px, `md` 20 px, `lg` 24 px; without it the spinner is 1.25em, sized with the text.

props.name: label
props.description: What is happening, announced politely ("Loading invoices"); without it the spinner is decorative.

components.notes:
It turns in the text colour. Without `label` it is decorative
(`aria-hidden`); with one it is a `status` that announces the label
politely. `size` is `sm` (16 px), `md` (20 px) or `lg` (24 px); without it
the spinner is 1.25em. Under reduced motion it turns slowly rather than
freezing, since a still ring reads as stuck.

import { Spinner, Stack } from '@weft/ui'
</script>

<template>
  <Stack direction="row" :gap="3" align="center">
    <Spinner label="Loading invoices" />
    <Spinner size="sm" />
    <Spinner size="lg" />
  </Stack>
</template>

components.name: Stack
components.purpose: Lays its children out in a column or a row with a gap from the spacing scale.
components.use: For any run of things one after another, a form's fields, a toolbar's buttons, a card's lines, instead of margins or a wrapper with its own CSS.
components.avoid: For columns that should reflow with the space available, use Grid; for a page or a titled part of one, use Page or Section.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; hit targets are the children's own.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; the gap scale is the same spacing tokens on landing and app.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; a row stays a row, so give it wrap when its children may not fit a narrow container.

props.name: direction
props.description: Lay the children out top to bottom (`column`) or along the line (`row`).

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between children, from the spacing scale (`--weft-space-*`).

props.name: align
props.description: Cross-axis alignment of the children.

props.name: justify
props.description: Main-axis distribution of the children; `between` pushes them to the ends.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Let a row wrap onto more lines when its children do not fit.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render, for semantics: `ul`, `nav`, `form`.

components.notes:
`gap` takes the spacing scale (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8, from `--weft-space-*`).
`align` and `justify` work along the cross and main axes as in flexbox, and
`as` renders another element, such as `ul` or `nav`, for the right semantics.

components.name: WeftProvider
components.purpose: Sets how the part of the page inside it is used, its input and its surface, for every Weft component within.
components.use: Around a layout to declare its surface (landing for marketing pages, app for tools), and to force an input for a kiosk, a preview or a test.
components.avoid: For choosing a component's look, use its own props; never use it to make a mobile version of something, since components adapt themselves.

adapts.input: Left unset, it passes on the browser's detected input, pointer or touch, live; set, it overrides it for everything inside.
adapts.surface: Left unset, it passes on the outer one (app by default); set, it switches density, type scale and spacing for everything inside.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; width comes from each component's own container.

props.name: input
props.description: Force `pointer` or `touch` for everything inside; unset passes on the detected or outer input.

props.name: surface
props.description: `landing` or `app` density for everything inside; unset passes on the outer surface.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render; it has `display: contents`, so it does not affect layout.

components.notes:
Its element carries `data-weft-input` and `data-weft-surface`, which the
theme's CSS reads to switch control heights, hit sizes and density. It renders
with `display: contents`, so it does not affect layout. Nested providers
override one axis and inherit the other.

<script setup vapor lang="ts">
import { Page, WeftProvider } from '@weft/ui'
</script>

<template>
  <WeftProvider surface="landing">
    <Page title="Ship faster" description="A landing page: wider type and spacing." />
  </WeftProvider>
</template>
